text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian employers and unions signed a new collective agreement which determines work benefits and will be valid for at least a year.

- Railway workers and management will continue talks on Tuesday within the frame of the new collective agreement. Workers said they will block cargo traffic from midnight if their demands for an increase in wages are not met.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said he expected parliament to start a debate on a constitutional change this week and believed the change would be carried out this month.
- Slovenia's third largest bank Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor (NKBM) said 1996 net profit rose to 1.95 billion tolars (12.4 million) from 1.76 billion a year before.
- April exports rose to $749.4 million from $669.8 million in March and from $723.4 million in April last year, the statistical office reported.
- A Hungarian military delegation visited their Slovenian colleagues in order to increase cross-border military cooperation.
